title: The roadmap upkeep list reads the live statuses, not "active"
why: The upkeep list is how triage sees a slip (step c55). It keys on status "active", which no step holds, so its stale and empty lists never fire and the ready count skips the "ready" steps.
source: retrospective 11:12 CST Nov 12, on the owner's question at 11:11 CST ("is triage even thinking though or is it just appending only?"); ruling c55 (owner Oct 26)
note: skills/roadmap/build.py upkeep() on main (line 1621, live = phases with an "active" step; ready list counts todo and active only). At roadmap 3b1a04109, 0 of 1,520 steps hold "active"; statuses in use: todo, ready, doing, blocked, queued, folded, done. Fix one home: main's skills/roadmap/build.py; the record branch's roadmap/build.py is a copy, so the lane says which one runs and drops the other or makes it call the first. Status names come from the one place the page defines them (KNOWN_STATUS, line 187), not a copy. todo and ready mean the same state (247 and 381 steps): flag it for one name. Red case first: a fixture with ready, todo and doing steps where the stale and empty lists must fire. Expect the first fixed run to list many steps; that is the slip c55 names, not a reason to loosen the check. Ready, no lane. Coordinator 12:13 CST Nov 12: #2825 at runner 10. After it merges, the record branch's roadmap/build.py becomes a wrapper that runs ~/.claude/skills/roadmap/build.py, and the record pre-commit dispatcher calls --check-staged (triage does this). Todo and ready are one state with two names (247 and 381 steps).
